description: Look things up in the shared knowledge base (read-only). The knowledge base is a tree of folders and .json files. Start with {"op":"read"} (the root): it shows what exists. A path is folder/file.json#/key/sub; keep the file extension. Every path that read, ls or find prints can be pasted back as path. read a folder or an object with an index = its description and its children; read a string = the text. Examples (in the stock knowledge everything about aos is under aos/): {"op":"read","path":"aos/errors.json"} ; {"op":"read","path":"aos/errors.json#/codes"} ; {"op":"ls","path":"aos/cli/"} lists children only ; {"op":"find","query":"timeout"} searches names, descriptions and text; a hit inside the text shows that line as [match: ...], so pick the hit whose line answers the question and read that path. Lines under 'not in index:' exist but have no description. Errors: NodeMissing (the line lists what exists there), PathBad, TargetBad (ls on text: use read; # on a non-.json file), KnowledgeMissing (no knowledge base is set up for you: say so), KnowledgeBad (the knowledge base set up for you is not a folder: say so).

op.description: read = show one place; ls = list the children of a folder or object; find = search by keyword and/or tag

path.description: Like aos/rules.json, aos/cli/ or aos/errors.json#/codes (# then the key inside the file; ~1 means / inside a key). Empty = the root. Copy paths exactly as read/ls/find print them. Do not start with / (that means an absolute file system path).

query.description: find: a word to look for (case-insensitive) in names, descriptions and text.

tag.description: find: an exact tag from the index entry's tags list. Give query, tag or both.

max_bytes.description: Most bytes to print (default 8000); longer output ends with [truncated: N more bytes].
